transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started with our coverage huddle. As we all know, the chemistry teacher will be out for five instructional days next week, and we have a draft plan that assigns Mr. Hall to all five chemistry periods with lab work postponed. Before I can approve and post this to the faculty coverage system, I need to hear from each of you with your operational reports. Please go ahead, one at a time.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue with this draft plan. My chemistry department calendar shows required practicals scheduled for Tuesday and Thursday of next week. State laboratory policy requires a certified chemistry teacher to be physically present for those labs. Ms. Nguyen is the only certified chemistry teacher available on both of those days. I updated the department calendar this week but have not yet forwarded it to the coverage system, which is likely why this scheduling conflict wasn't caught earlier.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a contract-limit issue I verified during this week's staffing audit. Human-resources records show that Mr. Hall's contract permits him to cover at most three class periods per day, while Ms. Nguyen's contract permits her to cover at most two class periods per day. I have not yet added these limits to the absence plan, which is likely why the draft assigning Mr. Hall to all five chemistry periods wasn't flagged for a contract violation.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise an urgent student-support concern. My graduation audit shows that four seniors must complete the chemistry practical before May 30. Their confirmed family transportation makes Friday from 3:30 to 4:30 p.m. the only available makeup window. I confirmed the transportation arrangements with the families this week, but I have not yet entered this window in the student-support calendar, which is likely why this constraint wasn't reflected in the draft plan.
transcript.speaker: A4
